title: Charles Skinner and why the film was embarrassing
summary: Barnet thought the producer insane when he proposed it, funded by ITT money; he found the finished film embarrassing for its montage of a girl dancing around New York, but likes the soundtrack.

story.theme_name: Jazz musicians in the movies and film scoring
story.community_name: Jazz musicians on film and studio scoring

blocks.x: Is he a New York person?

Well, he -- I did a short for him somewhere, and he came in Basin Street when we were making this thing -- when we were playing there -- and I thought he'd flipped his cookies, you know. He said, "I'm going to do this," and I was staying across the street at the Waldorf and he was calling there, and I told my wife, I said, "Please don't, I'm not here," when he calls, the man's insane. He wants to make an hour and 15 minutes of a band sitting there playing, in color, wide screen, stereophonic sound." And finally I got a call from Willard Alexander, he said, "Charlie, you better talk to Skinner. He just put the money up at the union. He really wants to do this." I said, "He put the money up at the union?" Yes, sure enough. But I thought the man was crazy, you know, because I couldn't conceive why anybody would spend all that money on me at that stage of the game. Particularly, I'd been out of the business a long time, and you know --
The band must have sounded good.
Well, it was a good band, I'll say that.
There was an interruption there. I checked back in the book listings and they don't know about that film that you made.
I didn't think they would, because like I say, it was never released and maybe it shouldn't have

been as a picture. I'm sorry to lose the soundtrack, but it -- I did see the thing in a viewing room up at 20th Century, a screening, you know, and if you look at it as moving picture entertainment, it's embarassing.

Well, because Charles Skinner, for some reason or other, decided right at the conclusion, which I had held at the beginning, that to take an hour and 15 minutes of a band would be so static, just a bunch of guys sitting there, that nobody would want to look at it.

Only band fans, but as a commercial thing I couldn't imagine anybody -- I found out, incidentally, later, that he got the money from ITT to do it. He was doing some commercial films for them and I guess he talked somebody into doing this. Let's put it this way, he's no longer with IT&T. I hope this wasn't the cause of it. But he superimposed one of those things with a girl running all over New York while the band is playing, and you know, a montage type thing, and it was embarassing, to look at it as a possible picture in a theater. I think that he might have cut it down to maybe a couple of half hour segments of the band playing, for program fillers here and there, and gotten away with it. But as an hour and 15 minutes -- and then he added, you know, another 15 minutes more onto the thing, so it became an hour and a half, with this girl running all over New York and
dancing in the streets, you know, and just distorted sky-scrapers and all that stuff. It was pretty corny.
The sound track I'd like to see out in records, though, because I was very happy with that.
